summary:
Supersedes the earlier version of this record, which could only describe the guest side. Home (the owner, read-only, live) has since confirmed the VMM device set (https://github.com/FS-GG/.github/issues/4517#issuecomment-6526676894); the facts below marked confirmed come from that comment and are not inferred. Re-confirm with Home before relying on them after any VMM change.

**Confirmed host-facing device set (Home, 2026-10-30)**
- **GPU:** `virtio-gpu-gl-pci` with blob resources, 4 GiB host memory window and **DRM native context**. It is not Venus and not virgl. Display is `egl-headless`. Only the **AMD integrated-GPU render node** is used; the host desktop renders on a separate discrete GPU.
- **Audio:** PipeWire audio backend, **output only** (emulated HDA controller with an output codec). There is **no capture** device.
- **Other devices:** virtio-net with user-mode networking and IPv6 off, virtio-rng. Machine is q35 with KVM.
- **VMM container:** devices are `/dev/kvm` plus the AMD render node only; all capabilities dropped and none added; no-new-privileges; read-only root filesystem; no restart policy; egress unchanged.

**Accepted risk.** DRM native context exposes the **host amdgpu kernel driver** to the guest, a wider attack surface than virgl. The owner accepted this under the VM-only security zone ruling (https://github.com/FS-GG/.github/issues/4778#issuecomment-6519522997; see environment/fdev-vm-is-the-only-security-zone). The VM, not in-guest tamper-proofing, is the security boundary. This record states the exposure; it does not remove it.

**Guest-side observations (Root/fdev live probe about 09:25 UTC on 2026-10-30; recheck before relying)**
- The guest sees a virtio GPU with a card node and a world-accessible render node; the developer account is in the video, render and audio groups.
- **Input (guest observation, not a Home statement):** Home's device list names no input device, and the guest shows only emulated PS/2 keyboard and mouse devices (live read of the guest input device list and virtio bus on 2026-10-30, with no virtio-input device). Treat "no virtio-input" as an inference from an absent entry plus that guest read; ask Home to confirm if it matters.
- Mesa 26.2.4 drives the host's real integrated AMD Radeon, not software rendering: Vulkan 1.4.354 via RADV (INTEGRATED_GPU); OpenGL 4.6 core and GLES 3.2 via radeonsi over EGL 1.5.
- Headless Chromium (`--headless=new --use-angle=vulkan --enable-features=Vulkan --ignore-gpu-blocklist`) gets a WebGL2 context on RADV; `--use-angle=gl` produced no WebGL2 context.
- **WebGPU is Unknown:** a headless `navigator.gpu` adapter probe returned nothing within 10 s.
- **Video decode is untested:** no `vainfo` or `ffmpeg` was installed.
- Audio: PipeWire 1.6.9 with the PulseAudio shim exposes one sink; a 1 s tone ran as a live stream and exited 0. Audibility on Home's speakers was not observed.

**What this enables:** hardware-accelerated testing inside fdev, such as browser WebGL2 render and switch tests (GAME-RENDER-MULTI-01), Vulkan and GL workloads, and audio playback paths, beyond SwiftShader-only evidence.

**Limits:** this is the host's shared integrated GPU, so timings are not dedicated-hardware or performance evidence. The guest-side probe is a live observation with no citable source file; the device-set facts rest on the Home confirmation comment cited above. Pausing: Home never pauses or freezes fdev; stop is an ACPI power-down on owner request only.
title: fdev GPU is virtio-gpu-gl with blob and DRM native context on the AMD iGPU render node only; audio is output-only PipeWire; input is emulated
